A production design system speeds up delivery and keeps accessibility a default. Pair unstyled accessible primitives with semantic tokens and you get a foundation that scales across products without rewriting the hard parts every quarter.

Accessible primitives

Primitives should own focus traps, keyboard navigation, and ARIA roles. You style the surface; behavior stays consistent out of the box so every product inherits the same interaction contract.

Tokens and theming

Keep colors, radius, and spacing in CSS variables. Light and dark modes swap tokens without shipping a theme runtime — consumers stay in control of the look while components stay portable.

Conclusion

Accessible behavior, flexible styling, and low runtime cost make a stack teams can adopt once and reuse everywhere.
